pages.PageText: Apex Mission Systems LLC Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Cover Letter and Certifications Offeror identification Legal name: Apex Mission Systems LLC Unique Entity ID (UEI): QX7F3K8L9MP2 CAGE code: 8AXM4 Address: 4100 Fairfax Ridge Pkwy, Suite 600, Fairfax, VA 22033 Representations and certifications The offeror certifies that its representations and certifications in SAM are current, accurate and complete as of the date of this proposal, and acknowledges all amendments to the solicitation. This proposal is valid for 120 days from the proposal due date for Enterprise IT Modernization Services. Signed: Dana Whitcomb, Chief Executive Officer

Apex Mission Systems LLC Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume I — Technical 1. Cloud Migration Methodology Apex will migrate the 140 mission applications in the Air Force cloud environment through our Migration Factory, a repeatable pipeline that discovers, assesses, refactors and cuts over each application in waves of 12 to 15 applications. The factory begins with automated discovery: dependency mapping agents run for 14 days against each application enclave and produce a migration blueprint covering data flows, ports, identities and integration points. Blueprints are peer reviewed by the Government product owner before a wave is scheduled. On our current Air Force Materiel Command migration task order, the factory has moved 61 applications with a measured mean migration time of 4 days per application from cutover rehearsal to production, and zero unplanned Sev-1 outages in the last 9 months. Each wave ends with a hypercare period of 10 business days in which the original application team and Apex site reliability engineers share an on-call rotation.

2. Cybersecurity and Continuous ATO Apex designs every migrated application to inherit controls from the Air Force cloud platform authorization and documents the remaining application-level controls in eMASS before cutover. After initial authorization, Apex maintains a continuous ATO. Automated control evidence collectors run daily, push results to eMASS, and open findings in the program's risk register within 24 hours of detection. The authorizing official receives a monthly control health summary. Container images are rebuilt weekly from hardened Iron Bank bases, scanned in the pipeline, and blocked from promotion on any critical vulnerability.

3. Legacy Application Rationalization Before migration, Apex scores every application on mission value, technical health and cost to run using the TIME model (tolerate, invest, migrate, eliminate). The rationalization board, chaired by the Government, decides the disposition of each application. On comparable programs this step retired or consolidated 18 to 22 percent of the portfolio before migration, avoiding the cost of moving applications with no remaining mission owner.

Apex Mission Systems LLC Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume II — Management 1. Staffing and Key Personnel Program Manager Marisol Ortega (PMP, 17 years) currently leads Apex's Air Force Materiel Command migration program of 85 staff. Cloud Architect Devin Park (AWS and Azure professional certifications, 12 years) is the technical authority for the factory. Both key personnel are current Apex employees and are committed full time from contract award. 2. Transition-In Plan Apex will complete transition-in within 45 days of award: knowledge transfer and shadowing in days 1 to 20, joint operations in days 21 to 40, and full assumption of responsibility by day 45, ahead of the required 60 days. 3. Risk Management Apex maintains a weekly risk review with the Government program office. Risks are scored on likelihood and impact, assigned an owner, and tracked to closure in a shared register.

Apex Mission Systems LLC Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume III — Past Performance Reference 1 — Air Force Materiel Command Application Migration (FA8730-22-F-0141) Value $31.2M, period 2022–present. Migration of 61 applications to Air Force cloud environments. CPARS 2024 and 2025: Exceptional in quality, schedule and management. Reference 2 — Space Systems Command DevSecOps Platform (FA8807-21-C-0077) Value $18.4M, period 2021–2025. Platform engineering and continuous ATO for 22 mission applications. CPARS 2025: Exceptional in quality, Very Good in cost control. Reference 3 — Defense Health Agency Hosting Consolidation (HT0011-20-F-0310) Value $9.7M, period 2020–2023. Consolidation of three data centers. CPARS final: Very Good.

Northstar Digital Partners Inc Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume I — Technical 1. Cloud Migration Methodology Northstar applies a six-phase migration lifecycle — assess, plan, build, test, cut over and optimize — tailored to each application's architecture. Assessment uses interviews with application owners and automated inventory scans. Applications are grouped into move groups by shared dependencies, and each move group follows a rehearsed cutover runbook. Northstar has migrated more than 200 workloads across federal civilian and defense customers, with an average move-group duration of six weeks.

2. Cybersecurity and Authorization Northstar's security engineers prepare the application security package, map inherited controls from the platform authorization, and support the authorizing official through the assessment and authorization process for each application. Our team includes Certified Information Systems Security Professionals who have supported more than 40 Air Force authorization packages to an initial ATO decision.

3. Legacy Application Rationalization Northstar will conduct a portfolio review in the first 90 days that recommends a disposition for each application: rehost, replatform, refactor, replace or retire.

Northstar Digital Partners Inc Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume II — Management 1. Staffing and Key Personnel Program Manager Ray Castellanos (PMP, 11 years) and Lead Architect Priya Raman (14 years) are committed to this effort. Northstar will recruit the remaining 60 percent of staff after award. 2. Transition-In Plan Northstar proposes a phased transition-in completed within 90 days of award, which allows time to recruit and clear the remaining staff before assuming full responsibility. 3. Risk Management Northstar tracks risks in a monthly report to the contracting officer's representative.

CivicWorks Technologies Corp Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume I — Technical 1. Cloud Migration Methodology CivicWorks will rehost each application to the Air Force cloud environment using a lift-and-shift approach that preserves the current architecture and minimizes change to the application teams. Our engineers manually rebuild each server in the target environment, copy application data during a scheduled maintenance window, and validate with the application owner before decommissioning the source. CivicWorks expects to complete migrations at a pace of six to eight applications per month.

2. Cybersecurity and Continuous ATO CivicWorks will maintain each application's existing security controls in the new environment and support continuous monitoring through quarterly vulnerability scans reported to the information system security manager.
3. Legacy Application Rationalization CivicWorks will migrate all 140 applications as currently configured so the Government can make rationalization decisions after the migration is complete.

CivicWorks Technologies Corp Proposal in response to Solicitation FA8771-27-R-0012 — Enterprise IT Modernization Services Department of the Air Force Volume II — Management 1. Transition-In Plan CivicWorks will complete transition-in within 60 days through an orientation period followed by joint operations. 3. Risk Management CivicWorks uses a risk log reviewed at monthly program management reviews.
